speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have a history of a painful, swollen left ankle that resolved on its own, and now your right knee is increasing in pain and swelling, along with episodes of pain when you urinate. To understand the connection between these symptoms, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or fever associated with the current knee swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient has been experiencing increasing pain and swelling in his right knee for the past 12 days. He reports pain with urination for the past 3 weeks and had a swollen, painful left ankle joint that resolved on its own about a week ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and using condoms inconsistently. He also reveals that his mother has rheumatoid arthritis. The patient appears anxious.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Reactive Arthritis (formerly Reiter's syndrome).

The combination of asymmetric oligoarthritis (ankle then knee), urethritis, and recent sexual activity with multiple partners strongly suggests this diagnosis. While his mother's rheumatoid arthritis is noted, it is less likely to cause the acute urethritis seen in this case.

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, HLA-B27, and Syphilis/HIV screening.
REQUEST IMAGES: Knee X-ray.
